answer: Each agent signs with a forward-secure quill: a hash ratchet that publishes the spent one-time key after every use, so a public vine of consumed keys grows in the open. At a random comet interval, many agents are challenged at once to extend that vine with the next signature in a few seconds. Shared ratchets collide on the same next key and merge under one reward cap; running N clones means keeping N secret ratchet states hot and answering N probes at once, or a missed extension is slashed.
